messages:
Alex: Quick sync — I'm leaning toward a hybrid admission model for Dedicated GPU pools: small guaranteed reservation + tokenized burst credits. want to align operator surface and control-plane APIs before writing code.
Priya: can you sketch tradeoffs? especially prewarm cost & tail latency.
Alex: sure. short bullets: 1) guaranteed slab = predictable throughput for high-SLA tenants. 2) burst credits let spiky workloads burst without overcommitting. 3) operator manages placement/eviction; control plane issues tokens and tracks balances. 4) need backpressure when credits exhausted, not hard rejects.
Marco: operator vs control-plane boundary concern — if operator enforces tokens, we need an idempotent token-redeem API. operator shouldn't hold complex accounting.
Sam: Agreed. Keep accounting in control plane (globally consistent ledger). operator gets lease intent with fields: desired_slab, burst_tokens_used, prewarm_hint. operator returns admit|queue.
Lila: telemetry question: what signals will determine automatic credit refill or decay? token-expiry? usage-window?
Alex: plan: sliding window burn rate + adaptive refill tied to recent SLA compliance. refill slower for tenants hitting tail latency.
Priya: prewarming cost: if we prewarm per token use we burn GPU time. suggest a cheap prewarm (low-priority warmers) first, then escalate to full prewarm only after sustained usage. :thinking_face: 
Marco: eviction order: 1) soft-evict idle burst sessions, 2) shrink guaranteed slab for opportunistic tenants (with notice), 3) preempt slab only as last resort. keep metrics to explain decisions in Console.
Sam: quick pseudo for admission flow: 
```
# control-plane
if tenant.tokens > 0 and pool.has_spare_slot():
  consume_token(); respond admit:burst
elif tenant.guarantee > 0 and pool.allocatable_for(tenant):
  respond admit:guarantee
else:
  respond queue_with_backoff()
```
We need idempotency keys for replays.
Lila: +1 on idempotency. Also add a signal that operator emits when prewarm completes so control-plane can mark request as served.
deploy-bot: Canary cluster updated: dedicated-orch/v2 -> canary-3, 2026-03-21T09:18:00Z :rocket:
Priya: we should run a sim with mixed workloads (steady enterprise + bursty PLG). Key metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per token, prewarm-hours consumed.
Alex: action items: 1) Marco to draft minimal token-redeem API (IDs + idempotency) by EOD tomorrow. 2) Sam to prototype admission pseudocode as an RFC. 3) Priya + Lila to design sim scenarios and telemetry signals. I'll consolidate into an RFC follow-up.
Marco: noted. will include failure modes (operator offline, control-plane partition) and fallback: degrade to best-effort queue and conservative slab admission.
Sam: also add a cheap-canary policy: allow small burst for new tenants with probation tokens to measure noisiness.
Lila: will add dashboards for token burn, prewarm-hours, and tail-latency per tenant.
Alex: thanks — let's review RFC draft next Tue. :thumbsup:
